boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a skeletal spirit who dismisses classes to residence-hall songs and a Coca-Cola welcome, these documented rituals mark the Emory calendar.

cards.title: When a Skeleton Dismisses Class
cards.subtitle: Emory’s resident spirit presides over a spring week of events
cards.notes: Watch for Lord Dooley and his entourage; bring a well-written limerick if you hope the university’s skeletal spirit will dismiss your class.
cards.short_summary: A costumed skeleton with a century-old campus persona becomes Emory’s unofficial authority for one spring week.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Dooley’s Week as a spring tradition hosted by the Student Programming Council, and says Dooley may cancel a class in exchange for a well-written limerick.
cards.access_notes: Participation and class-dismissal appearances depend on the current Dooley’s Week program.

cards.title: Wednesday Gets Its Own Campus Festival
cards.subtitle: Student groups take over the middle of the week
cards.notes: Walk through the scheduled gathering and browse the student-group tables; programming changes weekly, so check the university calendar first.
cards.short_summary: Emory turns an ordinary weekday into a recurring showcase for student organizations, activities and campus connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Wonderful Wednesday as a weekly event where student groups showcase what is happening, and its 2025 history traces the tradition’s evolution and revival.
cards.source_title: Magic of Midweek: The Evolution of Wonderful Wednesday
cards.access_notes: Consult Emory’s events calendar for the date, location and participation details of a particular week.

cards.title: Residence Halls Rewrite the Hits
cards.subtitle: First-years sing and dance for hall pride
cards.notes: Cheer for a residence hall or join its rehearsals if eligible; each team performs new lyrics and choreography set to familiar tunes.
cards.short_summary: Days after arriving, first-years turn residence-hall identity into a student-led musical competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory reports that Songfest began in 1984 and features first-year residence halls competing with original lyrics and choreography set to popular songs.
cards.source_title: Songfest celebrates 40th anniversary as beloved Emory tradition
cards.access_notes: Performance participation is for first-year residence halls; audience arrangements can vary by year.

cards.title: Enter Through the Gate, Then Raise a Coke
cards.subtitle: The incoming class crosses Emory’s threshold together
cards.notes: Line the route to cheer for incoming students, then follow the procession toward the Quad for the class’s first Coca-Cola toast.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial walk through the Haygood-Hopkins Gate leads directly into Emory’s orientation toast.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2024 fall guide says the Class of 2028 would cross the Emory gate, proceed to the Quad and participate in its first Coke Toast.
cards.source_title: 10 things to know for fall semester at Emory
cards.access_notes: The procession is tied to fall orientation; use the current welcome schedule for that year’s route and timing.

cards.title: Seniors Cross Over by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: A procession marks the shift from student to alum
cards.notes: Join the senior procession after finals and carry the ceremonial moment from the Emory Student Center toward the Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors physically cross campus together as their student chapter closes and alumni status begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 guide says seniors cross from students to alumni in a candlelight procession from the Emory Student Center to the Quadrangle after finals.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Held for graduating seniors before Commencement; the outdoor procession is weather permitting.

cards.title: Faculty Flip the Finals Script
cards.subtitle: Oxford instructors serve a late-night pancake meal
cards.notes: Take a study break at the announced finals meal and let Oxford faculty and staff handle the pancake service for the night.
cards.short_summary: During finals, the usual academic roles soften over stacks of pancakes served late at night.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s campus-culture page identifies Midnight Pancakes as a late-night finals meal served to Oxford College students by faculty and staff.
cards.access_notes: This Oxford College finals tradition is for students; confirm the semester’s date and entry details through campus announcements.

cards.title: The First Day Ends at a Carnival
cards.subtitle: Classes begin, then the Quad fills with rides and games
cards.notes: After the first day of classes, head to the announced Quad program for carnival rides, games, music and fair-style food.
cards.short_summary: Emory answers the first day’s academic intensity with a student-programmed evening carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists First Day Fest among its campus traditions and describes it as a first-day-of-classes carnival on the Quad with rides, games, music and fair-style food.
cards.access_notes: The event is scheduled around the first day of fall classes; verify current timing and attendance rules before going.

cards.title: One Bell Toll for Every Oxford Graduate
cards.subtitle: Commencement ends with a name-by-name count in sound
cards.notes: Remain after the Oxford recessional to hear the historic Seney Hall bell mark the graduating class one student at a time.
cards.short_summary: Oxford College translates its graduating-class roster into individual tolls from its historic bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 Commencement traditions guide says the historic Seney Hall bell tolls once for each Oxford College graduating student after the recessional.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: This occurs as part of Oxford College’s graduation ceremony; ceremony access requirements apply.

cards.title: Sign “MD” for the First Time
cards.subtitle: New physicians add their names during hooding
cards.notes: During the School of Medicine hooding ceremony, watch for graduates to enter the alumni book using their new credential.
cards.short_summary: Emory medical graduates make their new professional title tangible with a ceremonial signature.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says School of Medicine graduates sign the MD program alumni book during hooding, using the MD credential for the first time, a tradition dating to 1992.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to graduating MD students during the School of Medicine hooding ceremony.

cards.entity_name: Society of Corpus Cordis Aureum Procession
cards.title: Golden Eagles Lead the Graduates
cards.subtitle: Fifty-year alumni return in gold robes
cards.notes: At Commencement, look for alumni from classes of 50 or more years ago processing in gold ahead of the degree candidates.
cards.short_summary: Emory’s longest-tenured alumni visibly lead its newest graduates into Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 traditions guide says Society of Corpus Cordis Aureum members are alumni of 50 or more years who wear gold robes and lead degree candidates in the Commencement procession.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Procession participation is for eligible Society members; Commencement access requirements apply to observers.
